body:
Ok, after some looking around it appears the issue is the redirect to a non-active port.

Things I think we could do to make this work better...

1.  Restrict the scope to the service being scanned (ie. if we ask it to scan :443, it will not observe redirects and add them to the scan scope automatigally, maybe this is a prompt/alert the user somehow?).  As a user of ZAP, my expectation would be that we'd never scan the directed service due to scope restrictions and if were to redirect, then it would simply timeout and not halt the entire scan process.

2. Go fix this redirect behavior in Observatory, which I have raised with @april in https://github.com/mozilla/http-observatory-website/issues/138 (it seems this is the internal listening port)

issue.title: Favicon redirects to non-listening port
issue.body:
Repro: curl -k -i https://observatory.mozilla.org/images/favicons

Basically, https://observatory.mozilla.org/images/favicons redirects to http://observatory.mozilla.org:58443/images/favicons/ (the internal listening port, which is not publicly accessible)

rename.to: Spider/Active Scan Hangs scanning https://observatory.mozilla.org redirect to non-existent port

body: At the very least, ZAP should definitely not hang attempting to get the resource any longer than however long it or the webserver takes to timeout.

issue.title: Apply socket connect timeout

repository.name: zaproxy
repository.description: The ZAP by Checkmarx Core project

issue.body:
Change HttpSender to also set the socket connect timeout, to prevent ZAP
hanging when connecting.

Part of #4171 - Spider/Active Scan Hangs scanning
https://observatory.mozilla.org redirect to non-existent port

issue.title: Refactor redirection validation in active scans

repository.name: zaproxy
repository.description: The ZAP by Checkmarx Core project

issue.body:
Change AbtractPlugin and Analyser to use HostProcess to validate the
redirections, to reduce code duplication.
Change HostProcess to provide a HttpRedirectionValidator and a
HttpRequestConfig for validation of redirects.
Change HttpRedirectionValidator to have notifyMessageReceived as a
default method, the method is provided for convenience and not all
implementation require it, allowing the interface to be functional.
Change DefaultHttpRedirectionValidator to not implement the now default
method.

body: Closing, this should be addressed with #4173.
